activity_context.topic_title: Double Integrals Over Type I Regions

examples.knowledge_point: Evaluating a Repeated Integral Defined Over a Type I Region
examples.worked_solution:
The integral is defined over a type I region.

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $y$, treating $x$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{x}{x}^{2}y\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{x}y\,\text{d}y]\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}{[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{0}^{x}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}-0)\,dx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{4}\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $x\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{4}\,dx & =\frac{1}{2}{[\frac{{x}^{5}}{5}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{1}{5}-0) \\  & =\frac{1}{10}\end{aligned}
$$

If $D$ is the finite region enclosed by the lines $y=3-x,$ $y=0,$ and $x=0,$ as shown above, then ${∬}_{D}y{e}^{x}\,dA=$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, let's represent $D$ as a type I region. 

- To determine the $x$-limits, we need to find the $x$-coordinates of the points at which the curves intersect. So, we set the following equation and solve it for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3-x & =0 \\ x & =3\end{aligned}
$$

So, $x$-limits are 
$0\le x\le 3.$

- To determine the lower and upper functions, we draw a vertical arrow through the region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14100085/assets/479da73ff2382e584ec7eb02ff2517c7fa21322faf5ecbda2d2ff2d65049ef31.png)

As a result, we get

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 3,\,0\le y\le 3-x}.
$$

Therefore, we can express the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}y{e}^{x}\,dA & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{3-x}y{e}^{x}\,dy\,dx\end{aligned}
$$
